messages.text:
Morning,

We can give six students a decent stretch with someone's actual work in front of us if we keep this in the studio. The case for doing it elsewhere is that we could get a few more people in. The downside is we'd spend half the morning getting them there, and the two who have Friday shifts would be on a train by the time we started looking at anyone's work.

Callie has been speaking to the college. I've attached the rough running order she and I were working from, mostly so it's clear what the studio would be signing up to. I'd like each person to bring one piece they got stuck on, including the bits they cut. If we do polished decks again we easily lose the first hour to everyone trying to get their laptop to talk to the screen.

Can someone check if the big room is free from ten on 15 May? I've put Rupert on here because he offered us the small room at Merefurrow when we spoke about this in March.

Marcus

Marcus Adeyemi
Senior Product Designer, Acme Studio
acme.example

Hi all,

The six can all do 15 May from ten, but the college needs two of them back by half one. I can ask them to email a single piece the week before if that helps. One of them asked whether it could be a project they never finished and I said yes, which I think accounts for at least two of the sign-ups this morning. If you want to run through how we pair them up I can do Tuesday at 11:15 or Wednesday at 12:40.

Speak soon, Callie

Callie Fraser
Senior Consultant, Northlight Talent
+44 7700 900 231

Dear all,

The small room is free that Friday from half past nine, so we could put coffee out before you started. I am afraid the minibus is in use by the garden group that morning, though. To be back at the college by half past one they'd need to leave here shortly after eleven and the train from Faversham is no help if they miss it. If you can do this in London I expect the students will get a great deal more out of it there.

With kind regards,
Rupert Ashdown

The big room is booked, so let's stay on Turnmill Street. Thanks for offering the room, Rupert. I'd rather keep the six together until twelve and give the two who need to get back enough time to eat something.

Callie, yes to the unfinished piece. Can you tell them loose sheets are fine? Last time we made it sound like a job interview and one student brought the folder she'd already used for three interviews. She only showed us the work she actually wanted help with while we were walking her to the lift.

Marcus

Marcus Adeyemi
Senior Product Designer, Acme Studio
acme.example

truth.summary: Marcus kept the six-student portfolio morning at Acme after declining Rupert’s offer of a room at Merefurrow.

keyDates.what: Portfolio morning in Acme’s big room, starting at 10:00

facts: Two students need to be back at college by 13:30.
Students can bring unfinished work, and Marcus asked Callie to tell them loose sheets were fine.
